memory_update.text: For the election-sensitive public spending infrastructure node, keep PWR as the reference benchmark but prioritize smaller grid and utility field-service names such as MYRG for underfollowed follow-up.

NVEE is a permitting/compliance/program-management hypothesis: the market may miss infrastructure chokepoints that sit before construction, including utility services, conformity assessment, and mandated public-sector engineering work.
FSS is a municipal/public-safety equipment hypothesis: public works maintenance, warning systems, and specialized vehicles may be second-order beneficiaries of state/local spending resilience.

The node should be tracked through backlog quality, public-sector revenue mix, utility/customer concentration, master service agreements, skilled-labor constraints, and evidence of pass-through pricing rather than through election polling.

Need a later pass on border/security infrastructure suppliers, transformer component vendors, water/PFAS compliance utilities, and emergency communications software/hardware vendors; this pass focused on grid, permitting, public works, and municipal/public-safety equipment.

node: Election-sensitive public spending infrastructure: grid, security, permitting, and public works
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around policy-resilient public infrastructure spending rather than election outcomes. The reference anchor is Quanta Services because it is the obvious scaled grid-construction beneficiary. The underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller public companies with narrower exposure to grid hardening, utility field services, permitting/engineering, municipal public works, and public-safety equipment. These are research candidates only, not trading recommendations.
